Thailand with Kids
Family Trips Can Be Fun Too
intro: Thailand is an easy, warm place to travel with kids. Thai people love children, and most restaurants and hotels welcome families. There are shallow-water beaches, water parks, aquariums, and plenty of nature for kids to enjoy. This article rounds up the cities and activities that work well, where to stay, food kids will eat, and the health and safety basics parents should know.
quickAnswerHtml: Thailand is easy and safe to travel with kids — the culture adores children, and most hotels and restaurants are family-friendly. The best cities are Krabi/Khao Lak/Koh Samui (shallow beaches with gentle waves), Chiang Mai (cool weather, elephant camps, nature), and Bangkok (aquariums, theme parks). Mild food is easy to find, and private hospitals in the big cities are excellent. Medical emergency number 1669.

blocks.html: Good news for families: Thailand is one of the most relaxing places in Asia to travel with kids. Thai people are wonderful with children, restaurants and hotels often go out of their way to help, and you can find baby supplies (formula, diapers) easily in the cities. What you do need to plan for is choosing destinations that suit your kids' ages, keeping the pace relaxed, and looking after sun, mosquitoes, and drinking water.

blocks.text: Cities and Beaches That Work Well for Kids

items.name: Krabi / Khao Lak
items.blurb: Shallow beaches with gentle waves, great for kids to splash around. Lots of family resorts, and a more laid-back vibe than the party towns.

items.name: Koh Samui
items.blurb: Beautiful beaches and clear water, with both luxury and family resorts. Full facilities and direct flights.

items.name: Chiang Mai
items.blurb: Cool, comfortable weather, ethical elephant camps, cafés, and nature. Great for kids who don't like the heat.

items.name: Bangkok
items.blurb: Aquariums, zoos, water parks, children's museums, and malls with kids' zones. Easy to get around by BTS/MRT.

items: Splashing at shallow beaches + building sandcastles (pick bays with gentle waves)
Elephant camps focused on animal care (feeding, bathing elephants — choose no-riding options)
Aquariums and zoos in the big cities
Night markets and floating markets (snacks, shopping, fun to wander)

blocks.text: Where to Stay, Food, and Getting Around

blocks.title: Good to Know for a Smooth Trip

items.title: Family rooms
items.text: Many resorts have family rooms/extra beds, kids' pools, and kids' clubs. Confirm before you book.

items.title: Food for kids
items.text: Fried rice, chicken rice, noodles, omelets, and fruit are everywhere. Say "mai phet" (not spicy) and ask for chili on the side.

items.title: Car seats
items.text: Most taxis/Grab cars don't have car seats. If you need one, bring your own or book a vehicle that provides one in advance.

items.title: Baby supplies
items.text: Formula and diapers are easy to buy at malls/convenience stores in the cities. But sidewalks are uneven, so strollers are tricky — a baby carrier is easier.

blocks.html: The big cities have excellent private hospitals with pediatricians. The basics: reapply sunscreen often, drink bottled water, watch out for mosquitoes (use repellent, especially in the rainy season and in natural areas), and be careful of traffic and motorbikes on the roads. Medical emergency number 1669, tourist police 1155.

faq.q: Is Thailand suitable for traveling with young children?
faq.a: Very much so. Thai culture loves children, most hotels and restaurants are family-friendly, and baby supplies are easy to find in the cities. Pick destinations that suit your kids' ages and keep the pace relaxed, and you'll have an easy trip.

faq.q: Which beaches are safe for kids?
faq.a: Choose bays with gentle waves and shallow water — like many beaches in Krabi, Khao Lak, and Koh Samui, which have plenty of family resorts and a calmer atmosphere than the party towns. Check the monsoon season for each coast before you go.

faq.q: Is it easy to find food kids will eat?
faq.a: Very easy. Fried rice, chicken rice, noodles, omelets, and fruit are available everywhere. Tell the restaurant "mai phet" (not spicy) and ask for chili/dipping sauce on the side. Convenience stores have snacks and milk on every corner.

faq.q: Do I need to bring my own car seat?
faq.a: You should, if you need to use one, because most taxis and Grab cars don't provide car seats. Some rental car/transfer services have them available to book in advance — ask first.

faq.q: What health concerns should I watch out for?
faq.a: Reapply sunscreen often, drink bottled water, use mosquito repellent (especially in the rainy season and natural areas), and be careful of traffic. The big cities have excellent private hospitals and pediatricians. Medical emergency number 1669.
